items.text: We are to pray for the whole church of Christ upon earth; for magistrates, and ministers; for ourselves, our brethren, yea, our enemies; and for all sorts of men living, or that shall live hereafter; but not for the dead, nor for those that are known to have sinned the sin unto death.

items.title: For what things are we to pray?
items.text: We are to pray for all things tending to the glory of God, the welfare of the church, our own or others’ good; but not for anything that is unlawful.

items.title: How are we to pray?
items.text: We are to pray with an awful apprehension of the majesty of God, and deep sense of our own unworthiness, necessities, and sins; with penitent, thankful, and enlarged hearts; with understanding, faith, sincerity, fervency, love, and perseverance, waiting upon him, with humble submission to his will.

items.title: What rule hath God given for our direction in the duty of prayer?
items.text: The whole Word of God is of use to direct us in the duty of prayer; but the special rule of direction is that form of prayer which our Savior Christ taught his disciples, commonly called The Lord’s prayer.

items.title: How is the Lord’s prayer to be used?
items.text: The Lord’s prayer is not only for direction, as a pattern, according to which we are to make other prayers; but may also be used as a prayer, so that it be done with understanding, faith, reverence, and other graces necessary to the right performance of the duty of prayer.

items.title: Of how many parts doth the Lord’s prayer consist?
items.text: The Lord’s prayer consists of three parts; a preface, petitions, and a conclusion.

items.title: What doth the preface of the Lord’s prayer teach us?
items.text: The preface of the Lord’s prayer (contained in these words, Our Father which art in heaven) teacheth us, when we pray, to draw near to God with confidence of his fatherly goodness, and our interest therein; with reverence, and all other childlike dispositions, heavenly affections, and due apprehensions of his sovereign power, majesty, and gracious condescension: as also, to pray with and for others.

items.title: What do we pray for in the first petition?
items.text: In the first petition (which is, Hallowed be thy name), acknowledging the utter inability and indisposition that is in ourselves and all men to honor God aright, we pray, that God would by his grace enable and incline us and others to know, to acknowledge, and highly to esteem him, his titles, attributes, ordinances, word, works, and whatsoever he is pleased to make himself known by; and to glorify him in thought, word, and deed: that he would prevent and remove atheism, ignorance, idolatry, profaneness, and whatsoever is dishonorable to him; and, by his overruling providence, direct and dispose of all things to his own glory.

items.title: Q191 (1/2) · What do we pray for in the second petition?
items.text: In the second petition (which is, Thy kingdom come), acknowledging ourselves and all mankind to be by nature under the dominion of sin and Satan, we pray, that the kingdom of sin and Satan may be destroyed, the gospel propagated throughout the world, the Jews called, the fullness of the Gentiles brought in; the church furnished with all gospel officers and ordinances, purged from corruption, countenanced and maintained by the civil magistrate; that the ordinances of Christ may

items.title: Q191 (2/2) · What do we pray for in the second petition?
items.text: be purely dispensed, and made effectual to the converting of those that are yet in their sins, and the confirming, comforting, and building up of those that are already converted: that Christ would rule in our hearts here, and hasten the time of his second coming, and our reigning with him forever: and that he would be pleased so to exercise the kingdom of his power in all the world, as may best conduce to these ends.

items.title: What do we pray for in the third petition?
items.text: In the third petition (which is, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven), acknowledging that by nature we and all men are not only utterly unable and unwilling to know and to do the will of God, but prone to rebel against his word, to repine and murmur against his providence, and wholly inclined to do the will of the flesh, and of the devil: we pray, that God would by his Spirit take away from ourselves and others all blindness, weakness, indisposedness, and perverseness of heart; and by his grace make us able and willing to know, do, and submit to his will in all things, with the like humility, cheerfulness, faithfulness, diligence, zeal, sincerity, and constancy, as the angels do in heaven.

items.title: Q193 (1/2) · What do we pray for in the fourth petition?
items.text: In the fourth petition (which is, Give us this day our daily bread), acknowledging that in Adam, and by our own sin, we have forfeited our right to all the outward blessings of this life, and deserve to be wholly deprived of them by God, and to have them cursed to us in the use of them; and that neither they of themselves are able to sustain us, nor we to merit, or by our own industry to procure them; but prone to desire, get, and

items.title: Q193 (2/2) · What do we pray for in the fourth petition?
items.text: use them unlawfully: we pray for ourselves and others, that both they and we, waiting upon the providence of God from day to day in the use of lawful means, may, of his free gift, and as to his fatherly wisdom shall seem best, enjoy a competent portion of them; and have the same continued and blessed unto us in our holy and comfortable use of them, and contentment in them; and be kept from all things that are contrary to our temporal support and comfort.

items.title: What do we pray for in the fifth petition?
items.text: In the fifth petition (which is, Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors), acknowledging that we and all others are guilty both of original and actual sin, and thereby become debtors to the justice of God; and that neither we, nor any other creature, can make the least satisfaction for that debt: we pray for ourselves and others, that God of his free grace would, through the obedience and satisfaction of Christ, apprehended and applied by faith, acquit us both from the guilt and punishment of sin, accept us in his Beloved; continue his favor and grace to us, pardon our daily failings, and fill us with peace and joy, in giving us daily more and more assurance of forgiveness; which we are the rather emboldened to ask, and encouraged to expect, when we have this testimony in ourselves, that we from the heart forgive others their offenses.

items.title: Q195 (1/2) · What do we pray for in the sixth petition?
items.text: In the sixth petition (which is, And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil), acknowledging that the most wise, righteous, and gracious God, for divers holy and just ends, may so order things, that we may be assaulted, foiled, and for a time led captive by temptations; that Satan, the world, and the flesh, are ready powerfully to draw us aside, and ensnare us; and that we, even after the pardon of our sins, by reason of our corruption, weakness, and want of watchfulness, are not only subject to be tempted, and forward to expose ourselves unto temptations, but also of ourselves unable and unwilling to resist them, to recover out of them, and to improve them; and worthy to be

items.title: Q195 (2/2) · What do we pray for in the sixth petition?
items.text: left under the power of them; we pray, that God would so overrule the world and all in it, subdue the flesh, and restrain Satan, order all things, bestow and bless all means of grace, and quicken us to watchfulness in the use of them, that we and all his people may by his providence be kept from being tempted to sin; or, if tempted, that by his Spirit we may be powerfully supported and enabled to stand in the hour of temptation; or when fallen, raised again and recovered out of it, and have a sanctified use and improvement thereof: that our sanctification and salvation may be perfected, Satan trodden under our feet, and we fully freed from sin, temptation, and all evil, forever.

items.title: What doth the conclusion of the Lord’s prayer teach us?
items.text: The conclusion of the Lord’s prayer (which is, For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.) teacheth us to enforce our petitions with arguments, which are to be taken, not from any worthiness in ourselves, or in any other creature, but from God; and with our prayers to join praises, ascribing to God alone eternal sovereignty, omnipotency, and glorious excellency; in regard whereof, as he is able and willing to help us, so we by faith are emboldened to plead with him that he would, and quietly to rely upon him, that he will fulfill our requests. And, to testify this our desire and assurance, we say, Amen.

title: Baptist Catechism (Keach’s)
subtitle: 114 questions · 1693 tradition · 1695 printed edition
description: Historic Particular Baptist instruction in Christian faith, duty, prayer, and the ordinances.

items.title: Who is the First and Chiefest Being?
items.text: God is the First and Chiefest Being

items.title: Ought every One to believe there is a God?
items.text: Every One ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great Sin and Folly who do not.

items.title: How may we know there is a God?
items.text: The Light of Nature in Man, and the Works of God plainly declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit only, do it fully and effectually, for the Salvation of Sinners.

items.title: What is the Word of God?
items.text: The Holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments are the Word of God, and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience.

items.title: May all Men make use of the Holy Scriptures?
items.text: All Men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Holy Scriptures.

items.title: What things are chiefly contained in the Holy Scriptures?
items.text: The Holy Scriptures chiefly contain, what Man ought to believe concerning God, and what Duty God requireth of Man.

items.title: What is God?
items.text: God is a Spirit, Infinite, Eternal, and Unchangeable, in his Being, Wisdom, Power, Holiness, Justice, Goodness and Truth.

items.title: Are there more Gods than One?
items.text: There is but One only, the Living and True God.

items.title: How many Persons are there in the Godhead?
items.text: There are Three Persons in the Godhead, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; and these Three are One God, the same in Essence, equal in Power and Glory.

items.title: What are the Decrees of God?
items.text: The Decrees of God are, his Eternal Purpose according to the Counsel of his Will, whereby, for his own Glory, he hath foreordained whatsoever comes to pass.

items.title: How doth God execute his Decrees?
items.text: God executeth his Decrees in the Works of Creation and Providence

items.title: What is the Work of Creation?
items.text: The Work of Creation , is God's making all Things of Nothing, by the Word of his Power, in the space of six Days, and all very Good.

items.title: How did God create Man?
items.text: God created Man, Male and Female, after his own Image, in Knowledge, Righteousness and Holiness, with Dominion over the Creatures.

items.title: What are God's Works of Providence?
items.text: God's Works of Providence, are his most Holy, Wise, and Powerful preserving, and governing all his Creatures, and all their Actions.

items.title: What special Act of Providence did God exercise towards Man in the Estate wherein he was created?
items.text: When God had created Man, he entered into a Covenant of Life with him, upon Condition of perfect Obedience: forbidding him to eat of the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, upon pain of Death.

items.title: Did our first Parents continue in the Estate wherein they were created?
items.text: Our first Parents being left to the freedom of their own Will, fell from the Estate wherein they were created, by sinning against God.

items.title: What is Sin?
items.text: Sin is any want of Conformity unto, or Transgression of the Law of God.

items.title: What was the Sin whereby our first Parents fell from the Estate wherein they were created?
items.text: The Sin whereby our first Parents fell from the Estate wherein they were created, was their eating the forbidden Fruit.

items.title: Did all Mankind fall in Adam's first Transgression?
items.text: The Covenant being made with Adam, not only for himself, but for his Posterity, all Mankind descending from him by ordinary Generation, sinned in him, and fell with him in his first Transgression.

items.title: Into what Estate did the Fall bring Mankind?
items.text: The Fall brought Mankind into an Estate of Sin and Misery.

items.title: Wherein consists the sinfulness of that Estate whereinto Man fell?
items.text: The sinfulness of that Estate whereinto Man fell, consists in the Guilt of Adam's first Sin, the want of Original Righteousness, and the Corruption of his whole Nature, which is commonly called Original Sin; together with all actual Transgressions which proceed from it.

items.title: What is the Misery of that Estate whereinto Man fell?
items.text: All Mankind by their Fall lost Communion with God, are under his Wrath and Curse; and so make liable to all Miseries in this Life, to Death it self, and to the Pains of Hell for ever.

items.title: Did God leave all Mankind to perish in the Estate of Sin and Misery?
items.text: God, having out of his meer good pleasure, from all Eternity, elected some to Everlasting Life, did enter into a Covenant of Grace, to deliver them out of the Estate of Sin and Misery, and to bring them into an Estate of Salvation by a Redeemer.

items.title: Who is the Redeemer of God's Elect?
items.text: The only Redeemer of God's Elect, is the Lord Jesus Christ; who being the Eternal Son of God, became Man, and so was; and continueth to be God and Man, in two distinct Natures, and one Person for ever.

items.title: How did Christ, being the Son of God, become Man?
items.text: Christ the Son of God became Man, by taking to himself a true Body, and a reasonable Soul; being conceived by the Power of the Holy Spirit in the Womb of the Virgin Mary, and born of her, yet without Sin.

items.title: What Offices doth Christ execute as our Redeemer?
items.text: Christ as our Redeemer executeth the Offices of a Prophet, of a Priest, and of a King, both in his Estate of Humiliation and Exaltation.

items.title: How doth Christ execute the Office of a Prophet?
items.text: Christ executeth the Office of a Prophet, in revealing to us, by his Word and Spirit, the Will of God for our Salvation.

items.title: How doth Christ execute the Office of a Priest?
items.text: Christ executeth the Office of a Priest, in his once offering up of himself a Sacrifice to satisfy Divine Justice, and reconcile us to God, and in making continual Intercession for us.

items.title: How doth Christ execute the Office of a King?
items.text: Christ executeth the Office of a King, in subduing us to himself, in ruling, and defending us, and in restraining and conquering all his and our Enemies.

items.title: Wherein did Christ's Humiliation consist?
items.text: Christ's Humiliation consisted in his being born, and that in a low Condition; made under the Law, undergoing the Miseries of this Life, the Wrath of God, and the cursed Death of the Cross; in being buried, and continuing under the Power of Death for a time. Mat. 12:40.

items.title: Wherein consisteth Christ's Exaltation?
items.text: Christ's Exaltation consisteth in his rising again from the Dead on the third Day, in ascending up into Heaven, in sitting at the right Hand of God the Father, and in coming to judg the World at the last Day.

items.title: How are we made Partakers of the Redemption purchased by Christ?
items.text: We are made Partakers of the Redemption purchased by Christ, by the effectual Application of it to us by his Holy Spirit.

items.title: How doth the Spirit apply to us the Redemption purchased by Christ?
items.text: The Spirit applieth to us the Redemption purchased by Chrift, by working Faith in us, and thereby uniting us to Christ, in our effectual Calling.

items.title: What is effectual Calling?
items.text: Effectual Calling, is the Work of God's Spirit, whereby, convincing us of our Sin and Misery, enlightening our Minds in the knowledge of Christ, and renewing our Wills, he doth persuade and enable us to embrace Jesus Christ freely offered to us in the Gospel.

items.title: What Benefits do they that are effectually called, partake of in this Life?
items.text: They that are effectually called, do in this Life partake of Justification, Adoption, Sanctification, and the several Benefits which in this Life do either accompany or flow from them.

items.title: What is Justification?
items.text: Justification is an Act of God's free Grace, wherein he pardoneth all our Sins, and accepteth us as Righteous in his sight, only for the Righteousness of Christ imputed us, and received by Faith alone.

items.title: What is Adoption?
items.text: Adoption is an Act of God's free Grace, whereby we are received into the Number, and have a Right to all the Privileges of the Sons of God.

items.title: What is Sanctification?
items.text: Sanctification is the Work of God's free Grace, whereby we are renewed in the whole Man after the Image of God, and are enabled more and more to die unto Sin, and live unto Righteousness.

items.title: What are the Benefits which in this Life do accompany or flow from Justification, Adoption, and Sanctification?
items.text: The Benefits which in this Life do accompany or flow from Justification, Adoption, and Sanctification, are Assurance of God's Love, Peace of Conscience, Joy in the Holy Spirit, Increase of Grace, and Perseverance therein to the End.

items.title: What Benefits do Believers receive from Christ at their Death?
items.text: The Souls of Believers are at their Death made, perfect in Holiness, and do immediately pass into Glory: And their Bodies being still united to Christ, do rest in their Graves till the Refurrection.

items.title: What Benefits do Believers receive from Christ at the Resurrection?
items.text: At the Resurrection Believers being raised up in Glory, shall be openly acknowledged, and acquitted in the Day of Judgement, and made perfectly blessed, both in Soul and Body, in the full enjoyment of God, to all Eternity.

items.title: But what shall be done to the Wicked at their Death?
items.text: The Souls of the Wicked shall at their death be cast into the Torments of Hell, and their Bodies lie in their Graves, till the Refurrection and Judgment of the Great Day.

items.title: What shall be done to the Wicked at the Day of Judgment?
What is the Duty which God requireth of Man?
items.text: The Duty which God requireth of Man, is Obedience to his Revealed Will.

items.title: What did God at first reveal to Man for the Rule of his Obedience?
items.text: The Rule which God at first revealed to Man for his Obedience, was the Moral Law.

items.title: Where is the Moral Law summarily comprehended?
items.text: The Moral Law is summarily comprehended in the Ten Commandments.

items.title: What is the Sum of the Ten Commandments?
items.text: The Sum of the Ten Commandments is, to love the Lord our God, with all our Heart, with all our Soul, with all our Strength, and with all our Mind; and our Neighbour as our Selves.

items.title: What is the Preface to the Ten Commandments?
items.text: The Preface to the Ten Commandments, is in these words, "I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the Land of Egypt, out of the House of Bondage".

items.title: What doth the Preface to the Ten Commandments teach us?
items.text: The Preface to the Ten Commandments teacheth us, that because God is the LORD, and our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his Commandments.

items.title: Which is the first Commandment?
items.text: The first Commandment is, "Thou shalt have no other Gods before me".

items.title: What is required in the first Commandment?
items.text: The first Commandment requireth us, to know and acknowledge God to be the only true God, and our God; and to worship and glorify him accordingly.

items.title: What is forbidden in the first Commandment?
items.text: The first Commandment forbiddeth the denying, or not worshipping and glorifying the true God, as God, and our God; and the giving that Worship and Glory to any other, which is due unto him a alone.

items.title: What are we specially taught by these words "before me" in the first Commandment?
items.text: These words "before me" in the first Commandment, teach us, that God who seeth all things, taketh notice of, and is much displeased with the Sin of having any other God.

items.title: Which is the second Commandment?
items.text: The second Commandment is, "Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven Image, or any Likeness of any thing that is in Heaven above, or that is in the Earth beneath, or that is in the Water under the Earth; thou shalt not bow down thy self to them, nor serve them: For I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the Iniquity of the Fathers upon the Children, unto the Third and Fourth Generation of them that hate me; and shewing Mercy unto Thousands of them that love me and keep my Commandments.

items.title: What is required in the second Commandment?
items.text: The second Commandment requireth, the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances, as God hath appointed in his Word.

items.title: What is forbidden in the second Commandment?
items.text: The second Commandment forbiddeth the worshipping of God by Images, or any other Way not appointed in his Word.

items.title: What are the Reasons annexed to the second Commandment?
items.text: The Reasons annexed to the second Commandment are, God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he hath to his own Worship.

items.title: Which is the third Commandment?
items.text: The third Commandment is, "Thou shalt not take the Name of the Lord thy God in vain, For the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his Name in vain".

items.title: What is required in the third Commandment?
What is forbidden in the third Commandment?
What is the Reason annexed to the third Commandment?
items.text: The Reason annexed to the third Commandment, is, that however the breakers of this Commandment may escape Punishment from Men, yet the Lord our God will not suffer them to escape his Righteous Judgment.

items.title: Which is the fourth Commandment?
items.text: The fourth Commandment is, "Remember the Sabbath Day to keep it holy: Six Days shalt thou labour, and do all thy Work; but the Seventh Day is the Sabbath of the LORD thy God, in it thou shalt not do any Work, thou, nor thy Son, nor thy Daughter, thy Man-servant, nov thy Maid-servant, nor thy Cattel, nor the Stranger that is within thy Gates: For in six Days the LORD made Heaven and Earth, the Sea, and all that in them is, and rested the Seventh Day; wherefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath Day, and hallowed it".

items.title: What is required in the fourth Commandment?
items.text: The fourth Commandment requireth, the keeping Holy to God one whole Day in Seven, to be a Sabbath to himself

items.title: Which Day of the Seven hath God appointed to be the Weekly Sabbath?
items.text: Before the Refurrection of Christ, God appointed the Seventh Day of the Week to be the Weekly Sabbath, and the First Day of the Week ever since, to continue to the End of the World, which is the Christian Sabbath.

items.title: How is the Sabbath to be sanctified?
items.text: The Sabbath is to be sanctified by a holy Resting all that Day, even from such worldly Employments and Recreations as are lawful on other Days; and spending the whole Time in the Public and Private Exercises of God's Worship, except so much as is to be taken up in the Works of Necessity and Mercy.

items.title: What is forbidden in the fourth Commandment?
items.text: The fourth Commandment forbiddeth the Omission or careless Performance of the Duties required, and the profaning the Day by Idleness, or doing that which is in it self sinful; or by unnecessary Thoughts, Words, or Works about worldly Employments or Recreations.

items.title: What are the Reasons annexed to the fourth Commandment?
items.text: The Reasons annexed to the fourth Commandment, are God's allowing us six Days of the Week for our own lawful Employments, his challenging a special Propriety in a Seventh, his own Example, and his blessing the Sabbath Day.

items.title: Which is the fifth Commandment?
items.text: The fifth Commandment is, "Honour thy Father and thy Mother; that thy Days may be long upon the Land which the LORD thy God give it thee."

items.title: What is required in the fifth Commandment?
items.text: The fifth Commandment requireth the preserving the Honour, and performing the Duties belonging to every one in their several Places and Relations, as Superiours, Inferiors, or Equals.

items.title: What is forbidden in the fifth Commandment?
items.text: The fifth Commandment forbiddeth the neglecting of, or doing any thing against the Honor and Duty which belongeth to every one in their several Places and Relations.

items.title: What is the Reason annexed to the fifth Commandment?
items.text: The reason annexed to the fifth Commandment, is a Promise of long Life and Prosperity (as far as it shall serve for God's Glory, and their own Good) to all such as keep this Commandment.

items.title: What is the sixth Commandment?
items.text: The sixth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not kill".

items.title: What is required in the sixth Commandment?
items.text: The sixth Commandment requireth all lawful Endeavors to preserve our own Life, and the Life of others.

items.title: What is forbidden in the sixth Commandment?
items.text: The sixth Commandment absolutely forbiddeth the taking away of our own Life; or the Life of our Neighbor unjustly, or whatsoever tendeth thereunto.

items.title: Which is the seventh Commandment?
items.text: The seventh Commandment is, "Thou shalt not commit adultery".

items.title: What is required in the seventh Commandment?
items.text: The seventh Commandment requireth the Preservation of our own, and out Neighbor's Chastity, in Heart, Speech, and Behavior.

items.title: What is forbidden in the seventh Commandment?
items.text: The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.

items.title: Which is the eighth Commandment?
items.text: The eighth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not steal".

items.title: What is required in the eighth Commandment?
items.text: The eighth Commandment requireth the lawful procuring, and furthering the Wealth and outward Estate of our selves, and others.

items.title: What is forbidden in the eighth Commandment?
items.text: The eighth Commandment forbiddeth whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly hinder our own, or our Neighbour's Wealth, or outward Estate.

items.title: Which is the ninth Commandment?
items.text: The ninth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not bear false Witness against thy Neighbour".

items.title: What is required in the ninth Commandment?
items.text: The ninth Commandment requireth the maintaining and promoting of Truth between Man and Man, and of our own and our Neighbor's good Name, especially in Witness-bearing.

items.title: What is forbidden in the ninth Commandment?
items.text: The ninth Commandment forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to Truth, or injurious to our own or our Neighbor's good name.

items.title: Which is the tenth Commandment?
items.text: The tenth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not covet thy Neighbor's House, that shalt not covet thy Neighbor's Wife, nor his Man-servant, nor his Maid-servant, nor his Ox, nor his Ass, nor any thing that is thy Neighbor's".

items.title: What is required in the tenth Commandment?
items.text: The tenth Commandment requireth the full Contentment with our own Condition, with a right and charitable frame of Spirit toward our Neighbor, and all that is his.

items.title: What is forbidden in the tenth Commandment?
items.text: The tenth Commandment forbiddeth all Discontentment with our own Estate; envying or grieving at the Good of our Neighbor, and all inordinate Motions and Affections to any thing that is his.

items.title: Is any Man able perfectly to keep the Commandments of God?
items.text: No meer Man since the Fall, is able in this Life, perfectly to keep the Commandments of God, but doth daily break them, in Thought, Work, or Deed.

items.title: Are all Transgressions of the Law equally heinous?
items.text: Some Sins in themselves, and by reason of several Aggravations, are more heinous in the sight of God than others.

items.title: What doth every Sin deserve?
items.text: Every Sin deserveth God's Wrath and Curse, both in this Life, and that which is to come.

items.title: What doth God require of us, that we may escape his Wrath and Curse, due to us for Sin?
items.text: To escape the Wrath and Curse of God due to us for Sin, God requireth of us Faith in Jesus Christ, Repentance unto Life, with the diligent use all the outward Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption.

items.title: What is Faith in Jesus Christ?
items.text: Faith in Jesus Christ is a saving Grace, whereby we receive, and rest upon him alone for Salvation, as he is offered to us in the Gospel.

items.title: What is Repentance unto Life?
items.text: Repentance unto Life is a saving Grace, whereby a Sinner, out of a true Sense of his Sin, and Apprehension of the Mercy of God in Christ, doth, with grief and hatred of his Sin, turn from it unto God, with full Purpose of, and Endeavor after, new Obedience.

items.title: What are the outward Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption?
items.text: The outward in ordinary Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption, are his Ordinances, especially the Word, Baptism, the Lord's Supper, and Prayer; all which Means are made effectual to the Elect for Salvation.

items.title: How is the Word made effectual to Salvation?
items.text: The Spirit of God maketh the Reading, but especially the Preaching of the Word, an effectual Means of convincing and converting Sinners; and of building them up in Holiness and Comfort through Faith unto Salvation.

items.title: How is the Word to be read and heard, that it may become effectual to Salvation?
items.text: That the Word may become effectual to Salvation, we must attend thereunto with Diligence, Preparation, and Prayer; receive it with Faith and Love, lay it up in our Hearts, and practice it in our Lives.

items.title: How do Baptism and the Lord's Supper, become effectual Means of Salvation?
items.text: Baptism and the Lord's Supper become effectual Means of Salvation, not for any Virtue in them, or in him that doth administer them, but only by the Blessing of Christ, and the working of the Spirit in those that by Faith received them.

items.title: What is Baptism?
items.text: Baptism is an Ordinance of the New Testament instituted by Jesus Christ, to be unto the Party baptised, a Sign of his Fellowship with him, in his Death, Burial, and Resurrection; of his being ingrafted into him; of Remission of Sins; and of his giving up himself unto God through Jesus Christ, to live and walk in newness of Life.

items.title: To whom is Baptism to be administered?
items.text: Baptism is to be administered to all those, who actually profess Repentance toward God, Faith in, and Obedience to our Lord Jesus Christ, and to none other.

items.title: Are the Infants of such as are Professing Believers to be baptized?
items.text: The Infants of such as are professing Believers are not to be baptized, because there is neither Command, or Example in the Holy Scriptures, or certain Consequence from them to baptize such.

items.title: How is Baptism rightly administered?
items.text: Baptism is rightly administered, by Immersion, or dipping the whole Body of the Party in Water, into the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, according to Christ's Institution, and the Practice of the Apostles; and not by the sprinkling or pouring of Water, or dipping some Part of the Body, after the Tradition of Men.

items.title: What is the Duty of such who are rightly baptized?
items.text: It is the Duty of such who are rightly baptized, to give up themselves to some particular and orderly Church of Jesus Christ, that they may walk in all the Commandments and Ordinances of the Lord blameless.

items.title: What is the Lord's Supper?
items.text: The Lord's Supper is an Ordinance of the New Testament instituted by Jesus Christ; wherein by giving and receiving Bread and Wine, according to his Appointment, his Death is shewed forth; and the worthy Receivers are, not after a Corporal and Carnal manner, but by Faith, made Partakers of his Body and Blood, with all his Benefits, to their spiritual Nourishment, and growth in Grace.

items.title: Who are the proper Subjects of this Ordinance?
items.text: They who have been baptized upon a personal Profession of their Faith in Jesus Christ, and Repentance from dead Works.

items.title: What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper?
items.text: It is required of them that would worthily partake of the Lord's Supper, that they examine themselves, of their Knowledge to discern the Lord's Body, of their Faith to feed upon him, of their Repentance, Love, and new Obedience; lest coming unworthily, they eat and drink Judgment to themselves.

items.title: What is Prayer?
items.text: Prayer is an offering up our Desires to God, by the Assistance of the Holy Spirit, for things agreeable to his Will, in the Name of Christ believing, with Confession of our Sins, and thankful Acknowledgment of his Mercies.

items.title: What Rule hath God given for our Direction in Prayer?
items.text: The whole Word of God is of use to direct us in Prayer; but the special Rule of Direction is, that Prayer which Christ taught his Disciples, commonly called, The Lord's Prayer.

items.title: What doth the Preface of the Lord's Prayer teach us?
items.text: The Preface of the Lord's Prayer, which is, "Our Father which art in Heaven," teacheth us to draw near to God with all holy Reverence and Confidence, as Children to a Father, able and ready to help us; and that we should pray with and for others.

items.title: What do we pray for in the first Petition?
items.text: In the first Petition, which is, "Hallowed be thy Name," we pray, that God would enable us and others, to glorify him in all that, whereby he maketh himself known; and that he would dispose all things to his own Glory.

items.title: What do we pray for in the Second Petition?
items.text: In the second Petition, which is, "Thy Kingdom come," we pray that Satan's Kingdom may be destroyed, and that the Kingdom of Grace may be advanced, our selves and others brought into it and kept in it, and that the Kingdom of Glory may be hastened.

items.title: What do we pray for in the third Petition?
items.text: In the third Petition, which is, "Thy Will be done on Earth, as it is in Heaven," we pray, that God by his Grace would make us able and willing to know, obey, and submit to his Will in all things, as the Angels do in Heaven.

items.title: What do we pray for in the fourth Petition?
items.text: In the fourth Petition, which is, "Give us this Day our daily Bread," we pray, that of God's free Gift, we may receive a competent Portion of the good Things of this Life, and enjoy his Blessing with them.

items.title: What do we pray for in the fifth Petition?
items.text: In the fifth Petition, which is, "And forgive us our Debts as we forgive our Debtors," we pray, that God for Christ's sake would freely pardon all our Sins; which we are the rather encouraged to ask, because by his Grace we are enabled from the Heart to forgive others.

items.title: What do we pray for in the sixth Petition?
items.text: In the sixth Petition, which is, "And lead us not into Temptation, but deliver us from Evil," we pray that God would either keep us from being tempted to Sin, or support and deliver us when we are tempted.

items.title: What doth the Conclusion of the Lord's Prayer teach?
items.text: The Conclusion of the Lord's Prayer, which is, "For thine is the Kingdom, and the Power, and the Glory, for ever, Amen," teacheth us to take our Encouragement in Prayer from God only, and in our Prayers to praise him, ascribing Kingdom, Power and Glory to him: And in testimony of our Desire, and Assurance to be heard, we say, Amen.

title: Spurgeon’s Puritan Catechism
subtitle: 82 questions · 1855 historic English
description: Spurgeon’s concise Baptist adaptation of the Westminster and Baptist catechisms.

items.title: What is the chief end of man?
items.text: Man's chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him for ever

items.title: What rule has God given to direct us how we may glorify him?
items.text: The Word of God which is contained in the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments is the only rule to direct us how we may glorify God and enjoy him.

items.title: What do the Scriptures principally teach?
items.text: The Scriptures principally teach what man is to believe concerning God, and what duty God requires of man.

items.title: What is God?
items.text: God is Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable, in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth.

items.title: Are there more Gods than one?
items.text: There is but one only, the living and true God.

items.title: How many persons are there in the Godhead?
items.text: There are three persons in the Godhead, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one God, the same in essence, equal in power and glory.

items.title: What are the decrees of God?
items.text: The decrees of God are his eternal purpose according to the counsel of his own will, whereby for his own glory he has foreordained whatever comes to pass.

items.title: How does God execute his decrees?
items.text: God executes his decrees in the works of creation, and providence.

items.title: What is the work of creation?
items.text: The work of creation is God's making all things of nothing, by the Word of his power, in six normal consecutive days, and all very good.

items.title: How did God create man?
items.text: God created man, male and female, after his own image, in knowledge, righteousness, and holiness with dominion over the creatures.

items.title: What are God's works of providence?
items.text: God's works of providence are his most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all his creatures, and all their actions.

items.title: What special act of providence did God exercise toward man in the state wherein he was created?
items.text: When God had created man, he entered into a covenant of life with him, upon condition of perfect obedience, forbidding him to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, upon pain of death.

items.title: Did our first parents continue in the state wherein they were created?
items.text: Our first parents being left to the freedom of their own will, fell from the state wherein they were created, by sinning against God by eating the forbidden fruit.

items.title: What is sin?
items.text: Sin is any want of conformity to, or transgression of the law of God.

items.title: Did all mankind fall in Adam's first transgression?
items.text: The covenant being made with Adam, not only for himself but for his posterity, all mankind descending from him by ordinary generation, sinned in him, and fell with him in his first transgression.

items.title: Into what estate did the fall bring mankind?
items.text: The fall brought mankind into a state of sin and misery.

items.title: Wherein consists the sinfulness of that state whereinto man fell?
items.text: The sinfulness of that state whereinto man fell, consists in the guilt of Adam's first sin, the want of original righteousness, and the corruption of his whole nature, which is commonly called original sin, together with all actual transgressions which proceed from it.

items.title: What is the misery of that state whereinto man fell?
items.text: All mankind, by their fall, lost communion with God, are under his wrath and curse, and so made liable to all the miseries in this life, to death itself, and to the pains of hell for ever.

items.title: Did God leave all mankind to perish in the state of sin and misery?
items.text: God having, out of his good pleasure from all eternity, elected some to everlasting life did enter into a covenant of grace to deliver them out of the state of sin and misery, and to bring them into a state of salvation by a Redeemer.

items.title: Who is the Redeemer of God's elect?
items.text: The only Redeemer of God's elect is the Lord Jesus Christ, who being the eternal Son of God, became man and so was and continues to be God and man, in two distinct natures and one person for ever.

items.title: How did Christ, being the Son of God, become man?
items.text: Christ, the son of God, became man by taking to himself a true body and a reasonable soul, being conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit in the Virgin Mary, and born of her yet without sin.

items.title: What offices does Christ execute as our Redeemer?
items.text: Christ as our Redeemer executes the offices of a prophet, of a priest, and of a king, both in his state of humiliation and exaltation.

items.title: How does Christ execute the office of a prophet?
items.text: Christ executes the office of a prophet, in revealing to us, by his Word, and Spirit, the will of God for our salvation.

items.title: How does Christ execute the office of a priest?
items.text: Christ executes the office of a priest, in his once offering up himself a sacrifice to satisfy divine justice, and to reconcile us to God and in making continual intercession for us.

items.title: How does Christ execute the office of a king?
items.text: Christ executes the office of a king in subduing us to himself, in ruling and defending us and in restraining and conquering all his and our enemies.

items.title: Wherein did Christ's humiliation consist?
items.text: Christ's humiliation consisted in his being born, and that in a low condition made under the law, undergoing the miseries of this life, the wrath of God, and the cursed death of the cross; in being buried, and continuing under the power of death for a time.

items.title: Wherein consists Christ's exaltation?
items.text: Christ's exaltation consists in his rising again from the dead on the third day, in ascending up into heaven, and sitting at the right hand of God the Father, and in coming to judge the world at the last day.

items.title: How are we made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ?
items.text: We are made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ, by the effectual application of it to us by his Holy Spirit.

items.title: How does the Spirit apply to us the redemption purchased by Christ?
items.text: The Spirit applies to us the redemption purchased by Christ, by working faith in us and by it uniting us to Christ in our effectual calling.

items.title: What is effectual calling?
items.text: Effectual calling is the work of God's Spirit whereby, convincing us of our sin and misery, enlightening our minds in the knowledge of Christ, and renewing our wills, he does persuade and enable us to embrace Jesus Christ freely offered to us in the gospel.

items.title: What benefits do they who are effectually called, partake of in this life?
items.text: They who are effectually called, do in this life partake of justification, adoption, sanctification, and the various benefits which in this life do either accompany, or flow from them.

items.title: What is justification?
items.text: Justification is an act of God's free grace, wherein he pardons all our sins, and accepts us as righteous in his sight only for the righteousness of Christ imputed to us, and received by faith alone.

items.title: What is adoption?
items.text: Adoption is an act of God's free grace whereby we are received into the number, and have a right to all the privileges of the sons of God.

items.title: What is sanctification?
items.text: Sanctification is the work of God's Spirit whereby we are renewed in the whole man after the image of God and are enabled more and more to die to sin, and live to righteousness.

items.title: What are the benefits which in this life do either accompany or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification?
items.text: The benefits which in this life do accompany or flow from justification, are assurance of God's love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, increase of grace, perseverance in it to the end.

items.title: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at their death?
items.text: The souls of believers are at their death made perfect in holiness and do immediately pass into glory, and their bodies, being still united to Christ do rest in their graves till the resurrection.

items.title: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at the resurrection?
items.text: At the resurrection, believers being raised up in glory, shall be openly acknowledged and acquitted in the day of judgment, and made perfectly blessed both in soul and body in the full enjoying of God to all eternity.

items.title: What shall be done to the wicked at their death?
items.text: The souls of the wicked shall at their death be cast into the torments of hell, and their bodies lie in their graves till the resurrection and judgment of the great day.

items.title: What shall be done to the wicked at the day of judgment?
items.text: At the day of judgment the bodies of the wicked being raised out of their graves, shall be sentenced, together with their souls, to unspeakable torments with the devil and his angels for ever.

items.title: What did God reveal to man for the rule of his obedience?
items.text: The rule which God first revealed to man for his obedience is the moral law which is summarised in the ten commandments.

items.title: What is the sum of the ten commandments?
items.text: The sum of the ten commandments is to love the Lord our God with all our heart, with all our soul, with all our strength, and with all our mind; and our neighbour as ourselves.

items.title: Which is the first commandment?
items.text: The first commandment is, Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

items.title: What is required in the first commandment?
items.text: The first commandment requires us to know, and acknowledge God to be the only true God, and our God, and to worship and glorify him accordingly.

items.title: Which is the second commandment?
items.text: The second commandment is, "Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments."

items.title: What is required in the second commandment?
items.text: The second commandment requires the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious worship and ordinances as God has appointed in his Word.

items.title: What is forbidden in the second commandment?
items.text: The second commandment forbids the worshipping of God by images. or any other way not appointed in his Word.

items.title: Which is the third commandment?
items.text: The third commandment is, Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that takes his name in vain.

items.title: What is required in the third commandment?
items.text: The third commandment requires the holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, ordinances, Word, and works.

items.title: Which is the fourth commandment?
items.text: The fourth commandment is, Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: but the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor they cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates. For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the Lord blessed the Sabbath day and hallowed it.

items.title: What is required in the fourth commandment?
items.text: The fourth commandment requires the keeping holy to God such set times as he has appointed in his Word, expressly one whole day in seven, to be a holy Sabbath to himself.

items.title: How is the Sabbath to be sanctified?
items.text: The Sabbath is to be sanctified by a holy resting all that day, even from such worldly employments and recreations as are lawful on other days, and spending the whole time in the public and private exercises of God's worship, except so much as is taken up in the works of necessity and mercy.

items.title: Which is the fifth commandment?
items.text: The fifth commandment is, Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

items.title: What is required in the fifth commandment?
items.text: The fifth commandment requires the preserving the honour, and performing the duties belonging to every one in their various positions and relationships as superiors, inferiors, or equals.

items.title: What is the reason annexed to the fifth commandment?
items.text: The reason annexed to the fifth commandment is, a promise of long life and prosperity -- as far as it shall serve for God's glory, and their own good -- to all such as keep this commandment.

items.title: Which is the sixth commandment?
items.text: The sixth commandment is, Thou shalt not kill.

items.title: What is forbidden in the sixth commandment?
items.text: The sixth commandment forbids the taking away of our own life, or the life of our neighbour unjustly, or whatever tends to it.

items.title: Which is the seventh commandment?
items.text: The seventh commandment is, Thou shalt not commit adultery.

items.title: What is forbidden in the seventh commandment?
items.text: The seventh commandment forbids all unchaste thoughts, words, and actions.

items.title: Which is the eighth commandment?
items.text: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.

items.title: What is forbidden in the eighth commandment?
items.text: The eighth commandment forbids whatever does or may unjustly hinder our own or our neighbour's wealth, or outward estate.

items.title: Which is the ninth commandment?
items.text: The ninth commandment is, Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

items.title: What is required in the ninth commandment?
items.text: The ninth commandment requires the maintaining and promoting of truth between man and man, and of our own, and our neighbour's good name, especially in witness-bearing.

items.title: What is the tenth commandment?
items.text: The tenth commandment is, Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house; thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife,nor his manservant, or his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbour's.

items.title: What is forbidden in the tenth commandment?
items.text: The tenth commandment forbids all discontentment with our own estate, envying or grieving at the good of our neighbour, and all inordinate emotions and affections to anything that is his.

items.title: Is any man able perfectly to keep the commandments of God?
items.text: No mere man, since the fall, is able in his life perfectly to keep the commandments of God, but does daily break them in thought, word, and deed.

items.title: Are all transgressions of the law equally heinous?
items.text: Some sins in themselves, and by reason of various aggravations are more heinous in the sight of God than others.

items.title: What does every sin deserve?
items.text: Every sin deserves God's wrath and curse, both in this life and that which is to come.

items.title: How may we escape his wrath and curse due to us for sin?
items.text: To escape the wrath and curse of God due to us for sin, we must believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, trusting alone to his blood and righteousness. This faith is attended by repentance for the past, and leads to holiness in the future.

items.title: What is faith in Jesus Christ?
items.text: Faith in Jesus Christ is a saving grace, whereby we receive, and rest upon him alone for salvation, as he is set forth in the gospel.

items.title: What is repentance to life?
items.text: Repentance to life is a saving grace, whereby a sinner, out of a true sense of his sins, and apprehension of the mercy of God in Christ, does with grief and hatred of his sin turn from it to God, with full purpose to strive after new obedience.

items.title: What are the outward means whereby the Holy Spirit communicates to us the benefits of redemption?
items.text: The outward and ordinary means whereby the Holy Spirit communicates to us the benefits of Christ's redemption, are the Word, by which souls are begotten to spiritual life; Baptism, the Lord's Supper, Prayer, and Meditation, by all which believers are further edified in their most holy faith.

items.title: How is the Word made effectual to salvation?
items.text: The Spirit of God makes the reading, but especially the preaching of the Word, an effectual means of convicting and converting sinners, and of building them up in holiness and comfort, through faith to salvation.

items.title: How is the Word to be read and heard that it may become effectual to salvation?
items.text: That the Word may become effectual to salvation, we must attend to it with diligence, and prayer receive it with faith, and love, lay it up into our hearts, and practise it in our lives.

items.title: How do Baptism and the Lord's Supper become spiritually helpful?
items.text: Baptism and the Lord's Supper become spiritually helpful, not from any virtue in them, or in him who does administer them, but only by the blessing of Christ and the working of the Spirit in those who by faith receive them.

items.title: What is Baptism?
items.text: Baptism is an ordinance of the New Testament, instituted by Jesus Christ to be to the person baptised a sign of his fellowship with him, in his death, and burial, and resurrection, of his being ingrafted into him, of remission of sins, and of his giving up himself to God through Jesus Christ, to live and walk in newness of life.

items.title: To whom is Baptism to be administered?
items.text: Baptism is to be administered to all those who actually profess repentance towards God, and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ, and to none other.

items.title: Are the infants of such as are professing to be baptised?
items.text: The infants of such as are professing believers are not to be baptised, because there is neither command nor example in the Holy Scriptures for their baptism.

items.title: How is baptism rightly administered?
items.text: Baptism is rightly administered by immersion, or dipping the whole body of the person in water, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, according to Christ's institution, and the practice of the apostles, and not by sprinkling or pouring of water, or dipping some part of the body, after the tradition of men.

items.title: What is the duty of such as are rightly baptized?
items.text: It is the duty of such as are rightly baptized, to give up themselves to some particular and orderly Church of Jesus Christ that they may walk in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.

items.title: What is the Lord's Supper?
items.text: The Lord's Supper is an ordinance of the New Testament, instituted by Jesus Christ; wherein, by giving and receiving bread and wine, according to his appointment, his death is shown forth, and the worthy receivers are, not after a corporeal and carnal manner, but by faith, made partakers of his body and blood, with all his benefits, to their spiritual nourishment, and growth in grace.

items.title: What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper?
items.text: It is required of them who would worthily partake of the Lord's Supper, that they examine themselves of their knowledge to discern the Lord's body, of their faith to feed upon him, of their repentance, love, and new obedience, lest coming unworthily, they eat and drink judgment to themselves.

items.title: What is meant by the words, until he come, which are used by the apostle Paul in reference to the Lord's Supper?
items.text: They plainly teach us that our Lord Jesus Christ will come a second time; which is the joy and hope of all believers.

title: Catechism for Young Children
subtitle: 145 questions · Joseph P. Engles · 1840 original
description: Simple questions and answers introducing children to the faith of the Westminster Shorter Catechism.

items.title: Who made you?
items.text: God.

items.title: What else did God make?
items.text: God made all things.

items.title: Why did God make you and all things?
items.text: For his own glory.

items.title: How can you glorify God?
items.text: By loving him and doing what he commands.

items.title: Why ought you to glorify God?
items.text: Because he made me and takes care of me.

items.title: Are there more gods than one?
items.text: There is only one God.

items.title: In how many persons does this one God exist?
items.text: In three persons.

items.title: What are they?
items.text: The Father, the Son and the Holy Ghost.

items.title: What is God?
items.text: God is a Spirit, and has not a body like men.

items.title: Where is God?
items.text: God is everywhere.

items.title: Can you see God?
items.text: No; I cannot see God, but he always sees me.

items.title: Does God know all things?
items.text: Yes; nothing can be hid from God.

items.title: Can God do all things?
items.text: Yes; God can do all his holy will.

items.title: Where do you learn how to love and obey God?
items.text: In the Bible alone.

items.title: Who wrote the Bible?
items.text: Holy men who were taught by the Holy Ghost.

items.title: Who were our first parents?
items.text: Adam and Eve.

items.title: Of what were our first parents made?
items.text: God made the body of Adam out of the ground, and formed Eve from the body of Adam.

items.title: What did God give Adam and Eve besides bodies?
items.text: He gave them souls that could never die.

items.title: Have you a soul as well as a body?
items.text: Yes; I have a soul that can never die.

items.title: How do you know that you have a soul?
items.text: Because I can think about God and the world to come.

items.title: In what condition did God make Adam and Eve?
items.text: He made them holy and happy.

items.title: What is a covenant?
items.text: An agreement between two or more persons.

items.title: What covenant did God make with Adam?
items.text: The covenant of works.

items.title: What was Adam bound to do by the covenant of works?
items.text: To obey God perfectly.

items.title: What did God promise in the covenant of works?
items.text: To reward Adam with life if he obeyed him.

items.title: What did God threaten in the covenant of works?
items.text: To punish Adam with death if he disobeyed.

items.title: Did Adam keep the covenant of works?
items.text: No; he sinned against God.

items.title: What is sin?
items.text: Sin is any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, the law of God.

items.title: What is meant by want of conformity?
items.text: Not being or doing what God requires.

items.title: What is meant by transgression?
items.text: Doing what God forbids.

items.title: What was the sin of our first parents?
items.text: Eating the forbidden fruit.

items.title: Who tempted them to this sin?
items.text: The devil tempted Eve, and she gave the fruit to Adam.

items.title: What befell our first parents when they had sinned?
items.text: Instead of being holy and happy, they became sinful and miserable.

items.title: Did Adam act for himself alone in the covenant of works?
items.text: No; he represented all his posterity.

items.title: What effect had the sin of Adam on all mankind?
items.text: All mankind are born in a state of sin and misery.

items.title: What is that sinful nature which we inherit from Adam called?
items.text: Original sin.

items.title: What does every sin deserve?
items.text: The wrath and curse of God.

items.title: Can any one go to heaven with this sinful nature?
items.text: No, our hearts must be changed before we can be fit for heaven.

items.title: What is a change of heart called?
items.text: Regeneration.

items.title: Who can change a sinner's heart?
items.text: The Holy Spirit alone.

items.title: Can any one be saved through the covenant of works?
items.text: None can be saved through the covenant of works.

items.title: Why can none be saved through the covenant of works?
items.text: Because all have broken it, and are condemned by it.

items.title: With whom did God the Father make the covenant of grace?
items.text: With Christ, his eternal Son.

items.title: Whom did Christ represent in the covenant of grace?
items.text: His elect people.

items.title: What did Christ undertake in the covenant of grace?
items.text: To keep the whole law for his people, and to suffer the punishment due to their sins.

items.title: Did our Lord Jesus Christ ever commit the least sin?
items.text: No; he was holy, harmless and undefiled.

items.title: How could the Son of God suffer?
items.text: Christ, the Son of God, became man that he might obey and suffer in our nature.

items.title: What is meant by the Atonement?
items.text: Christ's satisfying divine justice, by his sufferings and death, in the place of sinners.

items.title: What did God the Father undertake in the covenant of grace?
items.text: To justify and sanctify those for whom Christ should die.

items.title: What is justification?
items.text: It is God's forgiving sinners, and treating them as if they had never sinned.

items.title: What is sanctification?
items.text: It is God's making sinners holy in heart and conduct.

items.title: For whom did Christ obey and suffer?
items.text: For those whom the Father had given him.

items.title: What kind of life did Christ live on earth?
items.text: A life of poverty and suffering.

items.title: What kind of death did Christ die?
items.text: The painful and shameful death of the cross.

items.title: Who will be saved?
items.text: Only those who repent of sin, believe in Christ and lead holy lives.

items.title: What is it to repent?
items.text: To be sorry for sin, and to hate and forsake it because it is displeasing to God.

items.title: What is it to believe or have faith in Christ?
items.text: To trust in Christ alone for salvation.

items.title: Can you repent and believe in Christ by your own power?
items.text: No; I can do nothing good without the help of God's Holy Spirit.

items.title: How can you get the help of the Holy Spirit?
items.text: God has told us that we must pray to him for the Holy Spirit.

items.title: How long ago is it since Christ died?
items.text: More than eighteen hundred years.

items.title: How were pious persons saved before the coming of Christ if
items.text: By believing in a Saviour to come.

items.title: How did they show their faith?
items.text: By offering sacrifices on God's altar.

items.title: What did these sacrifices represent?
items.text: Christ, the Lamb of God, who was to die for sinners.

items.title: What offices has Christ?
items.text: Christ has three offices.

items.title: What are they?
items.text: The offices of a prophet, of a priest, and of a king.

items.title: How is Christ a prophet?
items.text: Because he teaches us the will of God.

items.title: How is Christ a priest?
items.text: Because he died for our sins and pleads with God for us.

items.title: How is Christ a king?
items.text: Because he rules over us and defends us.

items.title: Why do you need Christ as a prophet?
items.text: Because I am ignorant.

items.title: Why do you need Christ as a priest?
items.text: Because I am guilty.

items.title: Why do you need Christ as a king?
items.text: Because I am weak and helpless.

items.title: How many commandments did God give on Mount Sinai?
items.text: Ten commandments.

items.title: What are the ten commandments sometimes called?
items.text: The Decalogue.

items.title: What do the first four commandments teach?
items.text: Our duty to God.

items.title: What do the last six commandments teach?
items.text: Our duty to our fellow-men.

items.title: What is the sum of the ten commandments?
items.text: To love God with all my heart, and my neighbor as myself.

items.title: Who is your neighbor?
items.text: All my fellow-men are my neighbors.

items.title: Is God pleased with those who love and obey him?
items.text: Yes; he says, 'I love them that love me.'

items.title: Is God displeased with those who do not love and obey him?
items.text: Yes; 'God is angry with the wicked every day.'

items.title: What is the first commandment?
items.text: The first commandment is, Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

items.title: What does the first commandment teach us?
items.text: To worship God alone.

items.title: What is the second commandment?
items.text: The second commandment is, Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them; for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.

items.title: What does the second commandment teach us?
items.text: To worship God in a proper manner, and to avoid idolatry.

items.title: What is the third commandment?
items.text: The third commandment is, Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

items.title: What does the third commandment teach us?
items.text: To reverence God's name, word, and works.

items.title: What is the fourth commandment?
items.text: The fourth commandment is, Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labor and do all thy work; but the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy man-servant, nor thy maid-servant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates: for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested on the seventh day: wherefore the Lord blessed the Sabbath day, and hallowed it.

items.title: What does the fourth commandment teach us?
items.text: To keep the Sabbath holy.

items.title: What day of the week is the Christian Sabbath?
items.text: The first day of the week, called the Lord's day.

items.title: Why is it called the Lord's day?
items.text: Because on that day Christ rose from the dead.

items.title: How should the Sabbath be spent?
items.text: In prayer and praise, in hearing and reading God's word, and in doing good to our fellow-men.

items.title: What is the fifth commandment?
items.text: The fifth commandment is, Honor thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

items.title: What does the fifth commandment teach us?
items.text: To love and obey our parents and teachers.

items.title: What is the sixth commandment?
items.text: The sixth commandment is, Thou shalt not kill.

items.title: What does the sixth commandment teach us?
items.text: To avoid angry passions.

items.title: What is the seventh commandment?
items.text: The seventh commandment is, Thou shalt not commit adultery.

items.title: What does the seventh commandment teach us?
items.text: To be pure in heart, language, and conduct.

items.title: What is the eighth commandment?
items.text: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.

items.title: What does the eighth commandment teach us?
items.text: To be honest and industrious.

items.title: What is the ninth commandment?
items.text: The ninth commandment is, Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.

items.title: What does the ninth commandment teach us?
items.text: To tell the truth.

items.title: What is the tenth commandment?
items.text: The tenth commandment is, Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbor's.

items.title: What does the tenth commandment teach us?
items.text: To be content with our lot.

items.title: Can any man keep these ten commandments perfectly?
items.text: No mere man, since the fall of Adam, ever did or can keep the ten commandments perfectly.

items.title: Of what use are the ten commandments to us?
items.text: They teach us our duty, and show our need of a Saviour.

items.title: What is prayer?
items.text: Prayer is asking God for things which he has promised to give.

items.title: In whose name should we pray?
items.text: Only in the name of Christ.

items.title: What has Christ given us to teach us how to pray?
items.text: The Lord's Prayer.

items.title: Repeat the Lord's Prayer.
items.text: OUR FATHER WHICH ART IN HEAVEN, HALLOWED BE THY NAME. THY KINGDOM COME. THY WILL BE DONE IN EARTH, AS IT IS IN HEAVEN. GIVE US THIS DAY OUR DAILY BREAD; AND FORGIVE US OUR DEBTS, AS WE FORGIVE OUR DEBTORS; AND LEAD US NOT INTO TEMPTATION, BUT DELIVER US FROM EVIL. FOR THINE IS THE KINGDOM, AND THE POWER, AND THE GLORY, FOR EVER. AMEN.

items.title: How many petitions are there in the Lord's Prayer?
items.text: Six.

items.title: What is the first petition?
items.text: 'Hallowed be thy name.'

items.title: What do we pray for in the first petition?
items.text: That God's name may be honored by us and all men.

items.title: What is the second petition?
items.text: 'Thy kingdom come.'

items.title: What do we pray for in the second petition?
items.text: That the gospel may be preached in all the world, and believed and obeyed by us and all men.

items.title: What is the third petition?
items.text: 'Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.'

items.title: What do we pray for in the third petition?
items.text: That men on earth may serve God as the angels do in heaven.

items.title: What is the fourth petition?
items.text: 'Give us this day our daily bread.'

items.title: What do we pray for in the fourth petition?
items.text: That God would give us all things needful for our bodies and souls.

items.title: What is the fifth petition?
items.text: 'And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.'

items.title: What do we pray for in the fifth petition?
items.text: That God would pardon our sins for Christ's sake, and enable us to forgive those who have injured us.

items.title: What is the sixth petition?
items.text: 'And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.'

items.title: What do we pray for in the sixth petition?
items.text: That God would keep us from sin.

items.title: How many sacraments are there?
items.text: Two.

items.title: What are they?
items.text: Baptism and the Lord's Supper.

items.title: Who appointed these sacraments?
items.text: The Lord Jesus Christ.

items.title: Why did Christ appoint these sacraments?
items.text: To distinguish his disciples from the world, and to comfort and strengthen them.

items.title: What sign is used in baptism?
items.text: The washing with water.

items.title: What does this signify?
items.text: That we are cleansed from sin by the blood of Christ.

items.title: In whose name are we baptized?
items.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

items.title: Who are to be baptized?
items.text: Believers and their children.

items.title: Why should infants be baptized?
items.text: Because they have a sinful nature and need a Saviour.

items.title: Does Christ care for little children?
items.text: Yes; for he says, SUFFER THE LITTLE CHILDREN TO COME UNTO ME, AND FORBID THEM NOT, FOR OF SUCH IS THE KINGDOM OF HEAVEN.

items.title: To what does your baptism bind you?
items.text: To be a true follower of Christ.

items.title: What is the Lord's Supper?
items.text: The eating of bread and drinking of wine in remembrance of the sufferings and death of Christ.

items.title: What does the bread represent?
items.text: The body of Christ, broken for our sins.

items.title: What does the wine represent?
items.text: The blood of Christ, shed for our salvation.

items.title: Who should partake of the Lord's Supper?
items.text: Only those who repent of their sins, believe in Christ for salvation, and love their fellow-men.

items.title: Did Christ remain in the tomb after his crucifixion?
items.text: No; he rose from the tomb on the third day after his death.

items.title: Where is Christ now?
items.text: In heaven, interceding for sinners.

items.title: Will he come again?
items.text: Yes; at the last day Christ will come to judge the world.

items.title: What becomes of men at death?
items.text: The body returns to dust, and the soul goes into the world of spirits.

items.title: Will the bodies of the dead be raised to life again?
items.text: Yes; 'the trumpet shall sound and the dead shall be raised.'

items.title: What will become of the wicked in the day of judgment?
items.text: They shall be cast into hell.

items.title: What is hell?
items.text: A place of dreadful and endless torment.

items.title: What will become of the righteous?
items.text: They shall be taken to heaven.

items.title: What is heaven?
items.text: A glorious and happy place, where the righteous shall be for ever with the LORD.
